newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan approves US$73.7 mln in China investments.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan approves US$73.7 mln in China investments.

text.p: Taiwan's economics ministry said on Tuesday it approved 14 investment projects worth US$73.685 million for China.
The ministry said in a statement the projects were approved during a regular monthly review session on Tuesday.
The ministry agreed to let President Enterprises invest US$30 million to form an investment trust branch in Shanghai to oversee the company's US$900 million investments in China.
It also approved a US$12 million investment by Taiwan's China Motor to manufacture and sell trucks in the southern Fujian province.

Though all investments in China must be approved by the government and routed indirectly through Hong Kong or other third places, Taiwan remains concerned that its economy may become too dependent on China and hence politically vulnerable.
Taiwan banned all direct official contact with China at the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
Despite the ban, indirect commerce has flourished since the late 1980s when political tensions started to thaw and some 30,000 Taiwan companies have poured more than US$20 billion into China so far.
